issues.t: Timing chain rattle on cold start
issues.sym: A rattle, whine or tapping from the front of the engine, loudest for the first few seconds after a cold start. Later a check engine light for cam timing can appear.
issues.why: The plastic timing chain guides and the tensioner on the 3.5L V6 wear with age and mileage, letting the chain slap around. Long oil change intervals speed this up.
issues.next: Have a shop listen to the engine on a cold start and check for cam timing codes. Fix it before the chain jumps a tooth, which can damage the engine.

issues.sym: Usually no warning signs. You may get a recall letter from Infiniti.
issues.why: The Takata passenger airbag inflators in these FX models can break apart when the bag deploys, after years of heat and humidity, and throw metal pieces into the cabin.
issues.next: Run your VIN on the NHTSA or Infiniti recall site. If the repair is open, book it right away; the dealer replaces the inflator free.

issues.sym: No symptoms. This affects some FX models that already had the passenger airbag replaced under an earlier recall.
issues.why: On certain 2003 and 2006-2008 FX35 and FX45 models, the replacement passenger airbag fitted under the earlier inflator recall could have been folded wrong, so it may tear when it inflates.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls, even if the earlier airbag recall was already done. The dealer fixes it free.

issues.sym: A humming, growling or roaring noise that rises with speed and may change when you steer left or right. In bad cases the ABS light can come on or the wheel feels loose.
issues.why: Wheel bearings on the FX wear out early. They are the most-reported repair on these SUVs in owner surveys, especially at the front.
issues.next: Have the wheels checked for play and noise. A worn bearing gets louder and can eventually fail, so do not leave it for long.

issues.sym: The top of the dashboard bubbles, swells, turns sticky or shiny and can make glare on the windshield.
issues.why: The dash covering used on first-generation FX models breaks down with heat and sunlight. Infiniti once offered a free repair program for it, which has since ended.
issues.next: Ask an Infiniti dealer with your VIN whether any goodwill help is left. Otherwise a dash cover or a replacement dash pad are the options.

issues.sym: A smell of gas or fuel dripping near the fuel filler, mostly while filling up.
issues.why: The rubber hose between the fuel filler neck and the tank could crack over time and leak fuel during refueling, which is a fire risk.
issues.next: Check for an open recall with your VIN. If you smell fuel, do not keep driving it; have the hose replaced.

issues.t: Front brake caliper bolts may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or knock from a front wheel when braking, or a pull to one side. In the worst case the brakes may not work properly.
issues.why: On some early 2003 FX models the bolts that hold the front brake calipers were not tightened enough at the factory, so a caliper could come loose.
issues.next: Make sure the recall was done. If you hear a knock when braking, stop driving and have the brakes checked.

issues.sym: A clunk or vibration from under the SUV, especially when pulling away or changing speed.
issues.why: On some 2003 FX models the bolts holding the driveshaft were not tightened enough at the factory, so the shaft could come loose.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. Any new clunk or vibration from underneath should be checked before you drive further.

issues.sym: The airbag light stays on or flashes on the dash.
issues.why: A failed airbag system sensor or a wiring fault causes the light. Owners report paying several hundred dollars for a sensor to fix it.
issues.next: Have the airbag codes read. The airbags may not work correctly while the light is on, so do not ignore it.

issues.sym: Oil seeping on the top or sides of the engine, a burning oil smell after driving, or oil getting into the spark plug wells and causing a misfire.
issues.why: The rubber valve cover gaskets and spark plug tube seals harden and crack with age. Owners often see leaks at around 70,000 to 90,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the leak confirmed and replace the gaskets and plug tube seals together. Fix it before oil reaches the coils or drips onto the exhaust.

issues.sym: Coolant puddles under the front of the SUV, a sweet smell, the coolant level dropping, or the temperature gauge climbing.
issues.why: The radiator, which has plastic end tanks, is one of the more common repairs on the FX and can crack or leak with age.
issues.next: Do not drive if the engine is overheating. Have the cooling system pressure-tested and replace the radiator if it is leaking.

issues.sym: You have to add oil between changes, see blue smoke from the exhaust, or the low oil light comes on.
issues.why: Some 4.5L V8 engines burn oil at high mileage, and owners point to worn piston rings or valve guides. One owner needed a replacement engine.
issues.next: Check the oil level every fill-up and keep track of how much you add. Have a compression and leak-down test done if it uses more than a quart every 1,000 miles or so.

issues.t: Stalling from a failing cam or crank sensor
issues.sym: The engine stalls, cuts out, runs rough or cranks without starting, often with a check engine light.
issues.why: Camshaft and crankshaft position sensors on these V6 and V8 engines fail with age and are a known repair on the FX.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Sensors are fairly cheap to replace, and a stall in traffic is dangerous.

issues.sym: Clunks over bumps, a loose or wandering feel, shaking when braking, or uneven tire wear.
issues.why: The rubber bushings in the control arms and tension struts wear out, letting the suspension move more than it should.
issues.next: Have the front suspension inspected. Worn arms are usually replaced in pairs, followed by an alignment.

issues.sym: Steering feels loose, the SUV wanders, there is a knock over bumps, or the front tires wear on the edges.
issues.why: The tie rod ends that connect the steering rack to the wheels wear out over time and are among the common FX repairs.
issues.next: Get the steering checked. Replace worn tie rod ends and get an alignment, since a failed one can affect control.

issues.sym: The SUV pulls to one side, a burning smell or heat from one wheel, or brake pads wearing out unevenly.
issues.why: A brake caliper can seize or its slide pins can stick, so the pads keep dragging on the rotor. Calipers are a frequent repair on the FX.
issues.next: If one wheel is much hotter than the others after driving, have the brakes checked soon. Replace the caliper and service the pins.

issues.sym: A metallic rattle from underneath at idle or low speeds, or a louder exhaust note.
issues.why: Exhaust heat shields rust and loosen, and the flex pipe and mid pipe can crack and leak.
issues.next: Have the exhaust looked at on a lift. Loose shields can often be clamped; a leaking flex pipe should be replaced.

issues.sym: An outside door handle feels loose, snaps or stops opening the door.
issues.why: The exterior door handles on the FX are a known weak point and break with use.
issues.next: Replace the handle. It is a simple repair, but paint-matched handles cost more.

issues.sym: One door will not lock or unlock with the remote or the switch, or the lock makes a buzzing noise.
issues.why: The electric lock actuator inside the door wears out.
issues.next: Replace the actuator in the affected door.

issues.sym: Extra play in the steering wheel or a clunk in the column. In the worst case steering control could be lost.
issues.why: On some 2009 FX models the steering column tube may not be perfectly round, which strains the upper bearing and can crack its retainer.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall and have it done. If the steering feels loose, do not drive it until it is checked.

issues.sym: Rough, late or jerky shifts, especially at low speeds or between the lower gears.
issues.why: Owners of second-generation FX models report shift quality problems with the 7-speed automatic. A software update (reflash) from the dealer usually fixes it.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check for transmission software updates before replacing parts. Also check the fluid condition.

issues.sym: The low oil pressure light flickers at idle, timing chain noise, or a check engine light for valve timing.
issues.why: On the 3.7L V6 a rubber gasket on the oil passage behind the timing cover can split and leak oil pressure inside the engine. Not much oil leaks out, but parts get less oil.
issues.next: Stop and check the oil level if the oil light flickers. A shop needs to remove the timing cover to replace the gasket, so it is best done before engine damage.

issues.sym: The steering wheel shakes and the brake pedal pulses when braking from highway speeds.
issues.why: Infiniti issued a service bulletin for brake judder on the QX70. It comes from uneven rotor thickness or runout.
issues.next: Have the rotors measured. Refinishing or replacing the rotors and checking hub runout usually cures it.

issues.t: Clicking from the axles when pulling away
issues.sym: A clicking or ticking noise from the front or rear wheels when you take off or accelerate.
issues.why: Infiniti published a bulletin for this noise, which comes from the drive axle joints at the wheel hub.
issues.next: Have a dealer confirm the source. The bulletin repair is a service of the axle-to-hub joint, not a full axle replacement.

issues.t: A/C blows warm from a refrigerant leak
issues.sym: The air conditioning gradually blows warmer and needs recharging again and again.
issues.why: Infiniti issued a bulletin for refrigerant leaks at the A/C pipe and hose joints, where damaged or dirty sealing surfaces let refrigerant escape.
issues.next: Have the system leak-tested with dye. Fixing the leaking joint is cheaper than repeated recharges.

issues.t: Check engine light for an EVAP leak
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with codes such as P0442, P0455 or P0456. The SUV drives normally.
issues.why: A small leak in the fuel vapor (EVAP) system, often at a hose, tube or the gas cap. Infiniti extended warranty coverage on an EVAP tube for some models.
issues.next: Make sure the gas cap clicks tight. If the light comes back, have a smoke test done and ask the dealer about warranty coverage.

issues.t: Water or fog inside the headlights
issues.sym: Condensation or water droplets inside a headlight lens, sometimes with dim or failed bulbs.
issues.why: Moisture gets past the headlight vents or seals. Infiniti published diagnostic steps for this.
issues.next: Have the headlight seal and vents checked. A cracked or badly sealed headlight usually needs to be replaced.

issues.t: ABS light on or brake fluid leak at the ABS unit
issues.sym: The ABS and brake warning lights come on, and you may see brake fluid near the ABS unit in the engine bay.
issues.why: Owners report the ABS actuator leaking brake fluid on the QX70. One owner reported that the leak caused an electrical fire.
issues.next: If you see brake fluid near the ABS unit or smell burning, park it and have it towed for inspection. Brake fluid leaks also lower braking performance.
